title: Dispatch: narrowed audit-fact finding registry (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch for eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15 (Foundation 2: truthful audit-fact registry
without executable membership claims). Attempt 1.

## What this is

PR #476 (head 9133201, branch eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6.10) reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED.
Part of its finding registry survived review as AUDIT FACTS; the rest made
executable-membership and zero-repeat claims that were not grounded. F2 salvages
only the surviving half and makes the artifact explicitly honest that it does not
ground the rest.

Nothing about this registry exists on `main` today. You are creating it fresh.

## Source material (read-only)

The #476 artifacts are reachable from this worktree's object store:

    git show 9133201:docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
    git show 9133201:docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
    git show 9133201:packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
    git show 9133201:packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

Do NOT check out that branch and do NOT copy those files wholesale. The #476 TS
module is 2112 lines and most of it is the invalidated machinery.

## Deliverables

1. `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json` (data)
2. `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md` (contract doc)
3. `packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts` (types + loader + validator)
4. `packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts` (tests)
5. export from `packages/core/src/internal.ts` ONLY — never `index.ts`
   (AGENTS.md: new core symbols default to internal)

## Row shape — EXACTLY these fields, no others

    {
      "canonicalId": "source-authority-opus-f19",
      "aliases": ["opus:F-19"],
      "invariant": "Composed spellPreparation source text is not presented as quotation",
      "status": "accepted",
      "statusReasoning": "…",              // optional; REQUIRED when status !== "accepted"
      "provenance": {
        "auditFinding": "opus:F-19",
        "evidenceBasis": "known-missing-source-clause"
      },
      "scopeKind": "clause",
      "owningBead": "eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1"
    }

Top level:

    { "version": 2, "explicitNonClaims": [ …strings… ], "rows": [ … ] }

## Mechanical transform from the #476 JSON

For each of the 68 rows, in the SAME ORDER as #476:

- `canonicalId`  <- `canonicalId` VERBATIM. These strings are cited elsewhere as
  labels naming prior defect classes; they must not be re-spelled.
- `aliases`      <- `aliases` VERBATIM (70 total across all rows).
- `invariant`    <- #476 `title` VERBATIM. See "Why title becomes invariant".
- `status`       <- `status` VERBATIM.
- `statusReasoning` <- `statusReasoning` VERBATIM where present (4 rows).
- `provenance.auditFinding` <- `obligation.authority` with the leading
  `audit-finding:` stripped. In all 68 rows the remainder is exactly one of that
  row's own aliases; assert this while transforming, do not paper over a miss.
- `provenance.evidenceBasis` <- `obligation.evidenceKind` VERBATIM.
- `scopeKind`    <- `target.kind` VERBATIM.
- `owningBead`   <- `owningBead` VERBATIM.

DROPPED ENTIRELY (see "Narrowing" below): `obligation.obligationId`,
`target.selector`, `baselineMembership`, `membershipStatus`, `underivedReason`,
`membershipDerivation`, `owningDerivationBead`, `violation`, `regression`,
`invariant` (the typed object), and every capability field.

Write a throwaway transform script under the scratchpad or `/tmp` to produce the
JSON, then DELETE it — it must not be committed. The committed JSON is the
artifact; there is no generator in-tree. Format the JSON with 2-space indent and
a trailing newline so Biome/format:check is stable.

`regression` is dropped because in all 68 rows `regression.locator ===
owningBead` and `regression.evidenceKind === "bead"` — it carried zero
information beyond `owningBead`. Say so in the doc.

## Why `title` becomes `invariant`

#476's typed `invariant` object was
`{kind:"source-semantic-preservation", dimensions:[branches,alternatives,timing,
lifecycle,termination], evidence:{kind:"audit-finding", locator:…}}` — and it was
BYTE-IDENTICAL across all 68 rows except for the locator. It carried no per-row
content. The actual per-row generalized invariant prose is the `title` string,
which is already phrased as a durable "what must remain true" statement
("Ki abilities and save DC are structured", "Madness durations are retained").

So F2 carries the prose forward under its honest name and drops the uniform
typed object. Do NOT invent new per-row prose — that would be source invention.
Disclose this collapse explicitly in the doc.

## Narrowing — the authority for what F2 must NOT contain

`bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15` carries two notes. The second one, "REVIEWER
DECISION 2026-07-28", SUPERSEDES the first. Read both; obey the second.

The decision: the executable membership fields move ENTIRELY to Foundation 3
(eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 / .19.1.8). Do NOT ship them as reserved-but-empty
placeholders — a reserved empty field still commits F2 to a membership SHAPE
that is F3's to define, and invites a later session to populate it unreviewed.

Removed entirely, not reserved:

1. `obligation.obligationId` — source-obligation identity is Foundation 1's, and
   #476 minted it from an audit-finding id (a category error). Replaced by
   `provenance` only.
2. `target.selector.members` -> F3
3. `baselineMembership` (whole field) -> F3
4. `membershipStatus` / `underivedReason` / `membershipDerivation`
5. `violation.queryId` / `violation.expectedAfterRepair`
6. `findingRegistryClosureReady()` / `findingRegistryClosureBlockers()`
7. `evaluateMembershipQuery`, `executeMembershipQuery`,
   `generateMembershipSnapshot`, `capabilityIdentit*ForHook`, `checkBeadReferences`,
   and every capability-membership field (capabilityId, canonical primitive,
   hookSelector, owning family epic) -> F4 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.16)
8. `invariant.dimensions` as a TYPED CHECKABLE contract — prose only.

Consequences for the TS module: it must NOT read `records.json`, must NOT read
the rules pack directory at all, must NOT shell out to `bd`, and must NOT import
`node:child_process`. Its only filesystem read is the registry JSON.

`scopeKind` survives as a plain descriptive label for what class of thing the
audit finding was about. It is NOT a selector and confers no membership. Say
that in both the doc and the type's doc comment.

## The acceptance criterion about separable fields

AC2 reads: "Audit fact, provenance, alias/status, owner, baseline membership,
current violation membership and closure evidence are separable fields."

The REVIEWER DECISION postdates and narrows it. Satisfy it as: the fields F2 DOES
keep are separable (audit fact / provenance / alias+status / owner are four
independent field groups, none derived from another), AND the doc states
explicitly that baseline membership, current violation membership, and closure
evidence are deliberately ABSENT and owned by Foundation 3, naming the beads. Do
not add empty fields for them. Do not silently ignore the criterion either —
address it in the doc under its own heading.

## `packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts`

Exports:

- `FindingStatus` = 'accepted' | 'rejected' | 'narrowed' | 'ambiguous' | 'disclosed-dependency'
  (the audit's full status vocabulary; only accepted/narrowed/disclosed-dependency occur today)
- `EvidenceBasis` = 'audit-finding' | 'source-span' | 'code' | 'bead' |
  'authoritative-input' | 'known-missing-source-clause'
  — doc comment MUST state this is a LOCAL descriptive vocabulary for how the
  audit fact was evidenced, and is deliberately NOT an identity shared with the
  clause-IR `EvidenceKind` union that Foundation 1 owns. No cross-PR identity claim.
- `FindingScopeKind` = 'record' | 'clause' | 'field' | 'path' | 'relationship' | 'capability'
- `FindingProvenance`, `FindingRow`, `FindingRegistry` interfaces
- `CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS` — the 68 canonicalIds as a readonly tuple, in registry order
- `FINDING_ALIASES` — the 70 aliases as a readonly tuple, sorted
- `loadFindingRegistry(path?)` — parses AND validates; throws on any violation
- `validateFindingRegistry(value: unknown): FindingRegistry` — the validator proper
- `aliasIndex(registry?)` -> `Map<string, FindingRow>`
- `findingByAlias(alias, registry?)`, `findingByCanonicalId(id, registry?)`

Default registry path resolves relative to `import.meta.url` as
`../../../../docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json`, which is
correct from both `src/rules/` and `dist/rules/`.

### Validator rules (each must throw a distinct, greppable message)

- `version` must be exactly 2.
- `explicitNonClaims` must be a non-empty array of non-empty strings.
- `rows` non-empty array of objects.
- `canonicalId` non-empty, matches `/^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/`.
- **Duplicate canonicalId is rejected.** (explicit acceptance criterion)
- The canonicalId set equals `CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS` exactly — reject both an
  omitted canonical row and an unexpected one, and report which.
- `aliases` non-empty; each matches `/^(opus|sol|fable|indep):[A-Za-z0-9-]+$/`.
- An alias may appear in at most one row (reject a duplicate across rows), and
  the union of all aliases equals `FINDING_ALIASES` exactly — so every alias
  resolves to exactly one row and none is lost.
- `invariant` non-empty string.
- `status` in the union; `statusReasoning`, when present, non-empty; and
  REQUIRED when `status !== 'accepted'`.
- `provenance.auditFinding` must be one of that row's own `aliases`.
- `provenance.evidenceBasis` in the union.
- `scopeKind` in the union.
- `owningBead` matches `/^eshyra-[A-Za-z0-9.]+$/`.
- **Forbidden-field guard.** Reject any row (or the top level) carrying any key
  from a deny-list: `obligation`, `target`, `selector`, `members`,
  `baselineMembership`, `membershipStatus`, `membershipDerivation`,
  `underivedReason`, `owningDerivationBead`, `violation`, `regression`,
  `capability`, `capabilityId`, `hookSelector`, `queryId`, `expectedAfterRepair`,
  `dimensions`, `closure`. Also reject any unknown key outright (strict shape).
  The deny-list is the belt-and-braces layer whose ERROR MESSAGE names
  Foundation 3 / Foundation 4 as the owner, so a future session that tries to
  repopulate membership here is told where it belongs instead of just "unknown
  key". This is what makes "no executable membership claim" mechanically
  enforced rather than a promise in prose.

Do not use `any`. Do not use non-null assertions. Narrow `unknown` explicitly —
the validator's whole job is that the on-disk bytes are untrusted.

## `packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts`

Import from `'../src/internal.js'` (see how neighbouring core tests do it and
match them). Cover at minimum:

- the real on-disk registry loads and validates
- exactly 68 rows, exactly 70 aliases, all aliases unique
- every alias resolves to exactly one row via `aliasIndex`
- `findingByAlias('opus:F-19')` and `findingByCanonicalId(...)` round-trip
- the four rows with `statusReasoning` keep their reasoning verbatim
- the one `narrowed` and two `disclosed-dependency` rows are present with reasoning
- version is 2 and `explicitNonClaims` is non-empty
- NEGATIVE: duplicate canonicalId throws
- NEGATIVE: duplicate alias across two rows throws
- NEGATIVE: missing canonical row throws; unexpected canonical row throws
- NEGATIVE: `provenance.auditFinding` not among the row's aliases throws
- NEGATIVE: non-accepted status without `statusReasoning` throws
- NEGATIVE: bad version throws
- NEGATIVE: each of a representative sample of deny-listed keys
  (`baselineMembership`, `target`, `violation`, `obligation`, `capabilityId`)
  throws, and the message names the owning Foundation
- NEGATIVE: an unknown key throws
- a structural test asserting the module source does NOT import
  `node:child_process` and does NOT reference `records.json` — this is the
  regression guard for the narrowing itself

Build negative fixtures by deep-cloning the real registry and mutating it, so a
fixture cannot drift from the real shape.

## `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md`

Rewrite from scratch — do not carry #476's doc, which asserts the invalidated
claims. Required sections:

- What this artifact IS: a registry of durable AUDIT FACTS — 68 canonical
  findings, 70 qualified aliases from four independent reviews (opus, sol,
  fable, indep) — preserved so the audit's conclusions survive the repair
  program.
- **What this artifact explicitly DOES NOT claim** (mirror `explicitNonClaims`):
  no executable exact membership; no derived or complete population for any
  finding; no zero-repeat / no-recurrence certification; no closure-readiness
  predicate; no capability-evidence claim; no assertion that the current pack
  does or does not violate any row. Name Foundation 3 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7,
  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8) and Foundation 4 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.16) as the owners.
- Field-by-field contract for the six row fields.
- The separability section addressing AC2 as described above.
- What was salvaged from #476 and what was dropped, with the reasons: the
  category-error `obligationId`, the uniform typed `invariant`, the redundant
  `regression`, and the whole membership/closure layer.
- Why the reviewer decision forbade reserved-but-empty placeholders.
- A pointer to the validator as the mechanical enforcement, including the
  deny-list.

Keep it under ~120 lines. No row data in the doc — the JSON is the source of
truth and duplicated row data drifts.

## Constraints

- Do NOT regenerate any rules pack. Do NOT touch `packages/core/data/`.
- Do NOT modify the freeze manifest. `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/` is a
  frozen prefix, but `THAW_NOTE_CHECK_ENABLED === false` for the duration of the
  eshyra-o9bd re-audit epic and neither new file is hash-pinned in
  `freeze-manifest.json`, so no thaw note is required. Do not add one.
- Do NOT weaken or edit any existing test.
- `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.
